title: Aus Minimum Wage 2026: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert the aus minimum wage 2026 of $26.44 per hour to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay. Includes tax, super and casual loading estimates.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38‑hour week, annual gross pay is approximately $52,254 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect the aus minimum wage 2026?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that means $33.05 per hour. This loading is intended to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When using the timesheet, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% to your base hourly rate – do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: What is the fortnightly pay for someone on the aus minimum wage 2026?
faqs.a: For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, the weekly pay is $1,004.90 (38 × $26.44). Fortnightly pay is double that: $2,009.80 before tax. After tax and Medicare levy, the take‑home amount will be lower – use the take‑home pay guide for a detailed estimate.

faqs.q: How much tax will I pay on the aus minimum wage 2026 annual salary?
faqs.a: Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, an annual gross salary of $52,254 falls into the 30% bracket (after the tax‑free threshold). Estimated tax is about $6,676 plus 2% Medicare levy ($1,045), leaving around $44,533 after tax and Medicare. This is an estimate only; your actual tax may differ if you have deductions or offsets.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Aus Minimum Wage 2026

The National Minimum Wage for 2026, as set by the Fair Work Commission, is **$26.44 per hour**. For a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, that works out to **$1,004.90 per week** and an annual gross salary of **$52,254** (26.44 × 38 × 52). This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many workers, however, are covered by an award that sets a higher minimum rate for their industry or occupation.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The basic formula is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38‑hour week because that is the standard full‑time week under the Fair Work Act. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the number accordingly. The timesheet on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and automatically calculates the annual, monthly, fortnightly and weekly figures. Remember to use your base rate – if you are a casual, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the floor. Most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their specific job type. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate than $26.44. Award rates also include penalty rates for weekends, evenings and public holidays, which are not factored into the simple hourly‑to‑annual conversion. If you are covered by an award, check your award’s pay rate – the [pay guides](/blog) page can help you find the right one.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that gives **$33.05 per hour** (26.44 × 1.25). This loading compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. When using the timesheet, do **not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading – instead, enter the base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator will add the 25% automatically.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

After tax and the Medicare levy, your fortnightly take‑home pay will be lower. See the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Super is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate for 2026–27 is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For someone earning the National Minimum Wage full‑time:

- Annual ordinary earnings: $52,254
- Super contribution (12%): $6,270.48

This super is not deducted from your pay – it is an additional amount your employer must pay into a super fund. The total cost to the employer is your gross pay plus super.

### Tax on the Aus Minimum Wage 2026

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For an annual salary of $52,254:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $52,254: ($52,254 – $45,000) × 30% = $2,176.20
- Total tax: $6,196.20
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,254): $1,045.08
- Total deductions: $7,241.28
- Estimated take‑home pay: $45,012.72 per year

This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may differ if you have tax offsets, deductions, or a HELP debt. The [reference tables](/data) page has more detailed tax calculations.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for May 2026:

- Full‑time adult ordinary time earnings: **$2,083.70 per week**
- All employees total earnings (including part‑time): **$1,579.20 per week**

These are averages across all industries and occupations, not medians. They are higher than the National Minimum Wage because they include higher‑paid roles. If you are comparing your pay to an industry average, note that it is an average, not a median for your specific job. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page explains how to interpret these figures.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is based on the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a personalised calculation, use the [timesheet](/). It lets you enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading if applicable, and see your annual, fortnightly and weekly figures with tax and super estimates.
